subject: CSA question set closure & scope adjudication — Acme Labs
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acmecorp.com>
Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CSA question set closure & scope adjudication — Acme Labs

Team,

Summary: I attached our latest CSA/CAIQ response bundle (CSA_responses_v1.3.pdf) and a working control answer log. Acme wants a final deliverable this week — they specifically asked for a clear scope adjudication & traceability matrix. Before I send, I need us to close the open items below and agree on which controls we mark in-scope vs out-of-scope under the managed-service boundary.

Open items (need owners):
- KMS / HSM attestation for customer-managed keys: who can provide the short attestation + procedure doc? (owner: kimberly_park)
- Tenant isolation narrative and runtime logs sample (2-week window): need a log sample export and short narrative for logical separation (owner: marissa_cole)
- Evidence pointer for continuous batching telemetry (control CCM-ML-05): we should point to the telemetry runbook and example trace IDs (owner: jordan_blake)

Proposed adjudication rules (draft; please push back):
1) Anything that requires customer-managed network appliances (on-prem) is out-of-scope.
2) Controls tied to model training data lineage (not inference runtime) are out-of-scope for this engagement.
3) Operational controls (auth, key rotation, telemetry) are in-scope and must have owner-level artifacts.

Timeline: can you each confirm your artifacts by EOD Tuesday 2027-05-11 PDT? I will compile and push a traceability matrix to the shared Drive and send to Acme on Wednesday.

Attachments: CSA_responses_v1.3.pdf (draft answers), control_answer_log.xlsx (workbook with per-control notes), scope_matrix.csv (proposed scope flags).

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Manager, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Acme Security <security@acmecorp.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CSA question set closure & scope adjudication — Acme Labs

Jordan — quick review notes inline and next steps. I pulled the control_answer_log.xlsx and made row-level comments for 14 controls; key highlights below.

Quick notes:
- Tenant isolation: we should provide a short architecture blurb (diagram link in Drive) + a 7-day auth/log sample rather than 2 weeks — Acme's request is reasonable but smaller sample will speed delivery. I flagged this in scope_matrix.csv as "in-scope: sample 7d".
- HSM attestation: kimberly, we will need a signed attestation (pdf) and the rotation cadence excerpt. If legal wants, include the KMS separation diagram.
- CCM-ML-05 (telemetry for batching): current answer is fine but needs two example trace IDs and one trace snippet (pseudonymized). I can mock the snippet from our staging traces — will you approve, Jordan?

Proposed scope edits (please comment):
- Reclassify CCM-DAT-02 (training data lineage) to out-of-scope per rule #2 above. I added a short rationale in the workbook.
- Keep CCM-ENV-03 (runtime environment hardening) in-scope but change evidence requirement from "full baseline report" to "hardening checklist + hardened image hash + nightly drift scan sample" — this is more actionable for them.

Owners: I can produce the log snippet and the environment hardening checklist by EOD Tuesday (2027-05-11). Kimberly to provide HSM attestation and a link to the artifact folder. Jordan to populate traceability matrix with the final answer IDs and the two telemetry trace IDs.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachment: control_answer_log.xlsx (comments tab)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CSA question set closure & scope adjudication — Acme Labs

Thanks — I'm on this.

Status: HSM attestation request sent to Infra-Sec (ticket #INFSEC-4221). They confirmed they can deliver a short attestation PDF and the key-rotation excerpt by Thursday morning (2027-05-13). I uploaded a preliminary scope_matrix.csv to the artifacts Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-TraceabilityMatrix.

Note: the attestation will state that customer-managed keys are supported when customers use our KMS integration and that the master key material is protected under an HSM-backed KMS. It will not include customer-specific key material (we cannot produce that).

I'll also add the HSM configuration snippet (redacted) to the Drive and update control_answer_log.xlsx with the attestation pointer. If Acme needs additional evidence for procurement, we can provide a signed statement from Infra-Sec + sample KM rotation logs (redacted).

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
Attachment: scope_matrix.csv (v0.2)

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmecorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acmecorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CSA question set closure & scope adjudication — Acme Labs

Jordan / team — thanks for the fast turnaround and for the clear owner list. A few clarifying points from Acme Security before you finalize: 

1) Traceability matrix: please include a linkable column for the exact artifact file (pdf/xlsx/csv) and an internal reference ID. That will let our audit team pull proofs quickly.
2) Logs sample: 7-day sample is ok; please ensure IPs are anonymized and session IDs are hashed.
3) HSM attestation: the signed attestation + rotation cadence excerpt will be sufficient for initial review. If procurement requests more, we'll escalate.

If you can send a consolidated package (CSA_responses_v1.3 + traceability matrix + highlighted attachments) by Wed EOD (your timezone) we'll schedule a short 30-min clarifying call on Thursday.

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Sr. Security Controls Manager
Acme Labs
